decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY confirming one $5 commission and one ticket per no-code primary mint, assigned together as a random reward package. Leaderboard and NFT-attribute accounting remains owned by the source Requirement.
The existing FAQ state already says no-code mints send the commission and tickets to a random existing NFT holder, and the source does not request a FAQ wording change.
The source explicitly reports that coded-referral rewards are already correctly accounted for and does not change the existing $5 commission and one-ticket award.
The client explicitly requires leaderboard totals to account for tickets and commissions from both coded referrals and randomly assigned no-code rewards.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
So far, we have done 12 mints, that should equal 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**When there is no referral code used, there is still a ticket and commission**.

Right now, **when a code is used**, it is correctly accounted for on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

When there is **no referral code used**, the ticket and commission are randomly assigned.
(B**ut they still need to be accounted for on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I think since your last fix, (on the last 2 mints) the randomly assigned tickets have been accounted for on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
But they have not been backfilled to show the missing tickets.

And the commissions (from these no code buys) are still not being accounted for on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot you'll see i have an NFT with 2 tickets and only 1 x $5 commission - this should be impossible, as every ticket comes with a $5 commission.

And on my leaderboard screenshot, you can count (from 12 total mints) 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions accounted for.
12 mints should equal 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions, regardless of a referral code being used or not.

value_updates.leaderboard_reward_totals: Leaderboard totals must include one ticket and one $5 commission for every primary mint, including rewards assigned randomly after a no-code mint.

decisions.reason: The existing no-code validation message already describes a $5 commission and $500 prize-draw ticket going to a random existing NFT holder; the source does not change that feedback text.
Accounting ticket and commission values on NFT attributes does not change the NFT mint number's role as its permanent referral code or its display locations.
The source establishes operational reward-accounting rules but does not request any landing-page mechanics copy change.
Referral ticket and commission accounting does not change prize payout mode, winner announcements, or winner notifications.
The source does not change the badge set, icons, count, or layout.
The source clarifies reward accounting and does not request a change to the hero title, mechanics tease, CTA, or emphasized selling points.
The accounting rule does not alter which NFT mint numbers are valid referral codes or the self-referral prevention rule.
The existing allocation already assigns a $5 referral commission per primary mint. The source changes reward-path accounting and recipient records, not the $15 revenue split.
